issuing_body: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)
covered_actors: Smart agricultural machinery manufacturers and vendors
Farmers and agricultural stakeholders (including producer groups, councils, extension advisors, and community farming organizations)
enforcement_authorities: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)
compliance_deadlines: FY2021 (Reiwa 3): Guideline compliance became a requirement for eligible MAFF subsidy programs

Prior to annual MAFF subsidy application submissions (calls typically open from January onward for the following fiscal year): Vendors must complete contract template revisions and publish compliance notices on websites or catalogs
penalties_summary: No statutory penalties are specified; in the event of a data leak after contracting under the guidelines, remedies such as damages are handled in accordance with the contractual terms agreed between the parties.
implementation_notes: This revised March 2024 Q&A clarifies compliance with MAFF's Contract Guidelines on AI and Data in the Agricultural Sector. Guideline compliance is required only as a condition for MAFF subsidy programs when introducing smart agricultural machinery, drones, robots, or IoT devices that transmit and store agricultural data on a service provider's server or cloud; self-funded deployments are outside the mandate, though compliance is recommended. System service providers verify compliance through self-assessment (consulting legal counsel and using MAFF's published checklist and model contracts) and disclose compliant products on websites or catalogs. Free contract consultation is available via INPIT's Intellectual Property Comprehensive Support Desks across all 47 prefectures.
